findings.note: A `cmd` node makes any workflow un-initializable with a real judge, and the error names a knob the operator never set. internal/fsm/kind/kind.go:609-610 registers the `cmd` kind with DefaultExec "fork", AllowedExec ["fork"] and ValidateParams: noParams, so a cmd node carries no model and no effort. internal/fsm/machine/machine.go:99-107 (Init) and :626-629 (Advance) call deps.Preflight for EVERY node whose Exec == "fork", with no kind discrimination. internal/fsm/cli/wiring.go:207-211 installs that Preflight as judge.Preflight(n.Model, n.Effort, ...) whenever `scenario == nil && mode == judgeReal`, and internal/fsm/judge/judge.go:267-269 rejects an empty model with ERR_JUDGE_MODEL{reason: length}. So `fsm init` on a workflow containing a cmd node fails before the --allow-custom-cmds consent gate is even reached, on every non-mock run. Meanwhile docs/fsm/driving-a-workflow.md:37 tells the operator that "`cmd` nodes run inside `advance`" under exec fork, docs/specs/2026-08-27-metareview-0.9.0-fsm-judge-kinds.md:233 declares `cmd {fork, [fork]}` with no model in its contract, and workflows/sdlc-loop.yaml:25-28 advertises the cmds/on_overflow escape hatch in a commented block. The documented escape hatch is unusable outside --mock-ai, and the operator is pointed at a judge model rather than at the real cause. No test drives a cmd node through Init or Advance (internal/fsm/kind/kind_test.go:631 exercises the executor directly), which is why every shard reads as internally consistent: the kind is in shard-2f-2, the preflight loop in shard-1c, the wiring in shard-09, the validator in shard-05, and the docs in shard-27 and shard-01.

findings.note: The git hardening that internal/fsm/gate/git.go established is absent from internal/gitcontext, which is the package that measures and cuts the diff every review actually reads. gate/git.go:209 and :221 pass --no-ext-diff (and --no-textconv) on both diff calls. Nothing in internal/gitcontext does: `--no-ext-diff` appears nowhere else in the tree. internal/gitcontext/branchfiles.go:107 and :129 run `git diff --no-renames --text --no-textconv <base>..HEAD -- <path>` - the invocation whose bytes become BranchFile.Diff, the shard chunks, the shard hashes and the byte budget - and branchfiles.go:37-41 sets cmd.Env only when extra entries are supplied, so the child inherits the full environment. internal/gitcontext/gitcontext.go:117, :121, :125, :140, :144 and :148 are worse: no --no-ext-diff, no --no-textconv, and git() at :332-334 sets no env at all. I proved the consequence rather than inferring it: in a scratch repo, `git config diff.external <script>` and, separately, `GIT_EXTERNAL_DIFF=<script>` each replaced the entire diff output of that exact argv with the driver's text, while the gate/git.go form with --no-ext-diff returned the real diff. A user with difftastic configured the documented way (`git config --global diff.external difft`) therefore gets shard packs containing difftastic output, deterministic lints scanning difftastic output, a byte budget measured from difftastic output, and a PASS over source nobody saw - silently, with no warning anywhere. The two wrappers are in different shards (gate/git.go in shard-0a, branchfiles.go in shard-0f, gitcontext.go in shard-22), so no per-shard reviewer sees that one of them was hardened and the other was not. Secondary inconsistency in the same seam: branchfiles.go passes --text while gitcontext.go does not, so the two byte measurements of the same repository can disagree by the full size of any binary file.

findings.note: The escalation rule stated to agents is not the predicate the code computes, and the owning spec agrees with the code rather than with the docs. internal/fsm/machine/fork.go:41-43 defines Escalated as `Attempt(snap) >= MaxAttempts && snap.Outcome != "" && !PassOutcome(snap.Outcome)` with Attempt = len(Lineage)+1 (fork.go:38) and MaxAttempts = 3 (fork.go:32); internal/fsm/record/record.go:70-74 stamps the runs.jsonl verdict on the same condition. The ancestors' outcomes are never consulted: the rule is 'lineage depth >= 3 AND this leaf is non-PASS', not 'three non-PASS attempts'. skills/fsm/SKILL.md:50 and docs/fsm/driving-a-workflow.md:78 both say 'three non-PASS attempts on one fork lineage', and fork.go:31's own comment repeats the wrong phrasing. docs/specs/2026-08-27-metareview-0.9.0-fsm-fork.md:313 states the real rule and mandates a test row for 'an attempt-4 non-PASS leaf (child of a PASS attempt-3 leaf)', confirming PASS runs are forkable and still count toward the depth. Judge-swap forking is an explicitly documented non-failure workflow (SKILL.md:47), so root -> judge-swap fork -> judge-swap fork reaches attempt 3, and if that third run ends non-PASS it is stamped ESCALATED and refused for further forking after exactly ONE failed attempt. An agent following SKILL.md treats that as impossible and will not relay the human stop the CLI is demanding. Independently: tests/go/test-fsm.sh contains no ERR_RUN_ESCALATED assertion anywhere, although docs/specs/2026-08-27-metareview-0.9.0-fsm-cli.md:315-316 mandates that black-box row - which is why the mismatch survived. Code in shard-1e, record in shard-02, SKILL in shard-32, doc in shard-27, spec in shard-20, suite in shard-3b.

findings.note: `metareview fsm state` - the documented recovery path when a driver does not know where a run is - fails for mock runs whose scenario directory has moved or been deleted, contradicting two explicit claims in its own spec. internal/fsm/cli/run.go:210-214 makes openRun call c.peek then c.scenarioFor and bail on error BEFORE machine.Open is reached at :219, and openRun is the entry point for state (run.go:396), gate --run (:682), converge --run (:853) and export (:923), all with readOnly = true. internal/fsm/cli/wiring.go:120-121 raises ERR_REPO_ROOT_MISMATCH there and :128 calls MockLoad. docs/specs/2026-08-27-metareview-0.9.0-fsm-cli.md:130-131 says 'ERR_REPO_ROOT_MISMATCH applies only to commands that need the scenario (advance, record, judge --run)', and :199-201 says state opens with OpenOptions{ReadOnly: true} 'so a concurrent fork advance, a re-pinned binary, or a removed scenario dir cannot make it fail'. The spec's reasoning is about the machine's load path; the CLI performs its own scenario read in front of it. For any run created with --mock-ai - every run the black-box suite drives - moving the checkout or deleting the scenario makes `fsm state` exit 2 with ERR_MOCK_INVALID / ERR_REPO_ROOT_MISMATCH instead of reporting where the run is, and internal/fsm/cli/prompt.go:7 is precisely the instruction that sends a driver there. Product runs are unaffected (wiring.go:117-118 returns early). CLI in shard-38, wiring in shard-09, spec in shard-08.

findings.note: The npm launcher's go-run fallback silently reviews the wrong repository. cli/metareview.js:15 sets `options = { cwd: process.cwd(), stdio: 'inherit' }` and the packaged-binary branch at :17-19 keeps it, but the fallback branch at :20-23 overwrites it with `{ cwd: root, stdio: 'inherit' }` where root = path.resolve(__dirname, '..'), the installed package directory. INSTALL.md:19 and :31-35, README.md:85-89, package.json:52 and cli/metareview.js:28's own error text all present the fallback as an equivalent runtime for a source checkout. findings.note: docs/fsm/sdlc-loop-example.md claims to be a real transcript and shows sequence numbers the machine cannot produce. The file states at :3-5 that it is 'exactly as the black-box suite drives it', then shows {"status":"OK","seq":5,"type":"node_output","key":"discover@0"} at :26 and forked_at_seq 9 / copied 8 at :54. The machine's actual order is init(1) at internal/fsm/machine/machine.go:199, tree(2) at :214, needs_input(3) at :679, node_output(4) at :984 - pinned as a literal sequence in internal/fsm/machine/machine_test.go:293 - and the CLI's runs.jsonl warning is envelope-only, not an event (internal/fsm/cli/run.go:329-332), so nothing can occupy the missing slot. discover@0's node_output is seq 4. Likewise the transition into fix cannot be at seq 9: discover alone consumes seqs 1-8 because nothing_found is evaluated and appended before findings_nonempty (workflows/sdlc-loop.yaml:10-11, machine.go:731-744), and adjudicate then adds llm_call, node_output, delta_applied, two gates and a transition. A driver that treats the example as ground truth will mis-read its own audit log. Example in shard-09, machine in shard-1c, the test that pins the real order in shard-2d-2.
